attribution.note: Zitron states in his own voice that Anthropic loses billions a year and that the AI labs are horribly unprofitable, presenting both as facts the Reuters article left out.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense factual assertion. The normalised version drops the media-criticism framing, which is not graded, and keeps both financial assertions.

contract.note: Reading 'billions' as at least $2B, using calendar 2025, and taking 'the AI labs' as Anthropic and OpenAI are ordinary plain readings. The result does not depend on the accounting basis: the GAAP loss ($42.0B) and the adjusted loss ($4.4B) both clear the threshold, and OpenAI's losses are large with or without the one-off charge.

evidence.note: Audited S-1 filed 2026-10-26, before the cutoff. It reports a 2025 net loss of $42.0B, of which $34.3B is a fair-value charge; the adjusted net loss is about $4.4B. Both exceed $2B. This is a company disclosure, but it is an audited admission of losses, the kind of source the contract prefers.
Reports OpenAI's 2025 operating loss of $20.92B and net loss of nearly $39B, from documents the FT reviewed. This shows substantial annual losses at the second lab.

The FT reports a 2025 net loss of about $39B, mostly a non-recurring non-cash charge, and about $8B excluding it. Even the underlying loss is substantial. Zitron first supplied the documents, but the FT independently corroborated them.
A projected Q2 2026 quarterly operating profit is a different period and metric from 2025 annual net loss, so it neither contradicts nor supports the claim.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's audited 2025 results show a net loss of $42.0B on a GAAP basis and $4.4B adjusted, both well above $2B; 2024 was also a multi-billion loss. OpenAI lost about $21B from operations in 2025 and about $8B even excluding non-cash items. Both labs had substantial annual losses on every basis shown. The projected Q2 2026 operating profit falls in a different period and metric, so it does not undercut the 2025 annual reading.
